threats.title: Stolen Pass
threats.description: Someone uses another member's pass, for example from a shared computer
threats.mitigation:
Passes expire after 12 hours and work on only one server.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 9.

threats.title: Deleted Abuse
threats.description: A member posts abuse, deletes it, and later denies it
threats.mitigation:
Messages are flagged as deleted instead of erased, and reports are saved on the Server.

PLANNED: Phase 6 Step 4 (deleting hides a message from members, but the owner can still read it until the retention period ends) and Step 7 (reports; the chat notice says deleted messages stay readable by the owner).

threats.title: Fake Hub
threats.description: The Server is tricked into talking to an impostor Hub
threats.mitigation:
The Hub's address is built into the Server, and it is HTTPS only.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Steps 8 and 10.

data.name: MusicBrainz

data.name: TMDB
data.reasonOutOfScope: Public metadata service run by someone else; Shogun only reads public data from it.

threats.title: Replayed Pass
threats.description: A server pass issued for a different server is replayed against this one
threats.mitigation:
Audience check: the pass must name this server; issuer and expiry are checked too.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 10 (JWT Bearer with the Hub as issuer and this server as audience; tests for wrong audience and expiry).

threats.title: Edited Role
threats.description: A member edits the role inside their pass to become the owner
threats.mitigation:
The pass signature is checked against the Hub's public key, so any edit breaks it.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 10 (signature check; a wrong-signature test).

threats.title: Owner-Only Endpoints
threats.description: A member calls endpoints meant for the owner, such as libraries, settings, or member permissions
threats.mitigation:
Endpoints are closed unless marked public; RequireOwner and RequireMember policies on every endpoint.

DONE: Phase 1B Step 5 (endpoints closed by default). PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 10 (RequireOwner and RequireMember policies).

threats.title: Other Members' Data
threats.description: A member changes another member's watch progress, messages, or comments by sending a different user ID (IDOR)
threats.mitigation:
The Server takes the user ID from the pass, never from the request body.

PLANNED: Phase 6 Steps 4-5 (the sender comes from the pass). PLANNED: Phase 3 Step 11 (the progress request carries no user ID; the Server takes the member from the pass).

threats.title: Library Permissions
threats.description: A member browses, searches, or streams a library they weren't given access to
threats.mitigation:
Library access is checked on browse, search, and stream.

PLANNED: Phase 3 Step 2 (stream endpoint checks the file's library) and Phase 6 Step 2 (per-member permissions).

threats.title: Removed Member
threats.description: A removed member keeps getting in with a server pass that has not expired yet
threats.mitigation:
Every request checks the local member table; membership syncs within about 2 minutes; chat disconnects removed members immediately.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 10 (member check and sync) and Phase 6 Step 5 (chat).

threats.title: Unauthenticated Info
threats.description: A stranger learns about the server without signing in
threats.mitigation:
Only the health endpoint is public, and it reveals very little.

DONE: Phase 1B Steps 5 and 7.

threats.title: Dishonest Owner
threats.description: The owner can see members' IP addresses, watch history, and chat on their own hardware
threats.mitigation: ACCEPTED RISK: cannot be prevented, because the data lives on the owner's machine. Be honest about it in the app (Phase 6 Step 7 chat notice) and never send Firebase login tokens to Servers (architecture.md section 3).

threats.title: Passes in Logs
threats.description: SignalR sends the server pass in the URL query string, so request logs can capture it
threats.mitigation:
Never log SignalR connection URLs.

PLANNED: Phase 6 Step 5 (and its Common mistakes list).

threats.title: Transcode Flood
threats.description: A member starts many transcodes at once and maxes out the CPU for everyone
threats.mitigation:
Separate limits for hardware and software transcodes; reply "server busy" instead of overloading.

PLANNED: Phase 3 Steps 5 and 7.

threats.title: Crafted Media File
threats.description: A booby-trapped media file exploits a bug in ffmpeg to run code on the owner's machine
threats.mitigation:
Keep ffmpeg updated with the Server image; run as a service user that can only read media; mount media read-only.

PLANNED: Phase 5 Step 4 (read-only media volume) and Step 5 (service user).

threats.title: Database Copies
threats.description: The database file or its backups expose the owner's TMDB key, chat, and member data
threats.mitigation:
Owner-only permissions on the data folder and on backups.

DONE: Phase 1B Step 6 (data folder). PLANNED: Phase 5 Step 9 (backups).

threats.title: Damaged Media
threats.description: A Server bug or exploit changes or deletes the owner's media
threats.mitigation:
Media mounted read-only; the service user can only read it.

PLANNED: Phase 5 Steps 4-5.

threats.description: A person using the app in their own browser
threats.mitigation: N/A: not network traffic. What the browser sends onward is covered on Shogun Web -> Shogun Server.

threats.title: Traffic in Transit
threats.description: Traffic between the browser and the Server is read or changed on the way
threats.mitigation:
HTTPS on the remote access network.

PLANNED: Phase 5 Step 6.

threats.title: Path Traversal
threats.description: A request containing ../../ reads files outside the media folders
threats.mitigation:
Files are looked up by MediaFile ID, never by a path; the resolved path must be inside a library root.

PLANNED: Phase 3 Step 2.

threats.title: Leaked Stream Link
threats.description: A signed stream URL gets shared and someone who is not a member plays it
threats.mitigation:
Signed stream URLs are short-lived and tied to one file.

PLANNED: Phase 3 Step 3.

threats.title: Chat Flood
threats.description: One member floods chat with messages
threats.mitigation:
More than 30 messages a minute blocks sending for 10 minutes.

PLANNED: Phase 6 Step 5.

threats.title: Claim Code in Logs
threats.description: Anyone who can read the console or logs sees the claim code
threats.mitigation:
The code expires in 30 minutes and works only once.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 6.

threats.title: Owner's Own Files
threats.description: The owner copies their own files into their own folders
threats.mitigation: N/A: the owner controls both ends. Harmful files are covered by Crafted Media File and Argument Injection.
